Moral Foundations Theory is a framework that separates human morality into the following categories:

  - Care/Harm: related to our long evolution as mammals with attachment systems
    and an ability to feel (and dislike) the pain of others. It underlies the
    virtues of kindness, gentleness, and nurturance.

  - Loyalty/Betrayal: related to our long history as tribal creatures able to
    form shifting coalitions. It is active anytime people feel that it is "one
    for all and all for one." It underlies the virtues of patriotism and
    self-sacrifice for the group.

  - Authority/Subversion: shaped by our long primate history of hierarchical
    social interactions. It underlies virtues of leadership and followership,
    including deference to prestigious authority figures and respect for
    traditions.

  - Sanctity/Purity: shaped by the psychology of disgust and contamination. It
    underlies notions of striving to live in an elevated, less carnal, more
    noble, and more "natural" way (often present in religious narratives). This
    foundation underlies the widespread idea that the body is a temple that can
    be desecrated by immoral activities and contaminants (an idea not unique to
    religious traditions). It underlies the virtues of self-discipline,
    self-improvement, naturalness, and spirituality.

  - Equality: related to our intuitions about equal treatment and equal outcome
    for individuals.

  - Proportionality: related to our intuitions about individuals getting
    rewarded in proportion to their merit or contribution.

Every category has a bidirectional nature. For example:

One person's sensitivity to the Care/Harm foundation may lead them to support high levels of immigration from poorer nations, to reduce the suffering of those who migrate. Whereas another person's sensitivity to the very same foundation may lead them to oppose those levels, because they believe it could lead to people they care about being harmed.

# Conservative Party Manifesto 2024: Summary

## Economic Policy

The manifesto outlines plans to reduce employee National Insurance from 12% to 6% by April 2027, representing a £1,350 annual reduction for average earners. Self-employed individuals would see their main National Insurance rate abolished entirely. The party commits to maintaining fiscal rules requiring public sector net debt to fall and borrowing to remain below 3% of GDP.

Business support includes maintaining corporation tax rates, extending "full expensing" to leasing when conditions allow, and a ten-point plan for SMEs covering business rates relief, VAT threshold reviews, and improved access to finance.

## Taxation and Pensions

The "Triple Lock Plus" would ensure State Pensions rise annually by the highest of inflation, earnings, or 2.5%, while introducing a new age-related personal allowance to prevent pensioners being drawn into income tax. Child Benefit reforms would move to a household-based system, with withdrawal beginning at £120,000 combined income.

## Immigration

Proposals include a legally binding annual cap on migration covering work and family visas, with Parliament voting on levels each year. The Rwanda removal scheme would continue, alongside reforms to asylum rules and increased visa fees. Health checks for migrants would be introduced, with potential Immigration Health Surcharge increases.

## Defence and Security

Defence spending would increase to 2.5% of GDP by 2030, with £10 billion invested in munitions production. Plans include continued Ukraine support, nuclear deterrent modernisation, and a National Defence and Resilience Plan.

## Healthcare

NHS spending would increase above inflation annually, with commitments to recruit 92,000 additional nurses and 28,000 doctors. Pharmacy First expansion, 250 new or modernised GP surgeries, and 50 Community Diagnostic Centres are planned. Social care cost caps would be implemented from October 2025.

## Housing

The target is 1.6 million new homes, achieved through brownfield development fast-tracking, planning reforms, and abolishing EU nutrient neutrality rules. First-time buyers would benefit from permanent Stamp Duty relief up to £425,000 and a new Help to Buy scheme.

## Education and Skills

Proposals include mandatory National Service for 18-year-olds (military or civic), 100,000 new apprenticeships funded by closing underperforming university courses, and the Advanced British Standard for 16-19 education. Mobile phones would be banned during school hours.

## Energy and Environment

Annual oil and gas licensing rounds would continue, alongside trebling offshore wind capacity and building Small Modular Reactors. Green levies on household bills would be kept lower than 2023 levels. Net zero by 2050 remains the target.

## Transport

£36 billion from HS2 savings would fund regional transport improvements, including £8.3 billion for road maintenance. The £2 bus fare cap would continue throughout the Parliament. Measures would prevent road pricing and reverse London's ULEZ expansion.

## Welfare Reform

Plans include reforming disability benefits assessment, tightening work capability assessments, and introducing stricter sanctions for those refusing suitable employment after 12 months. Projected savings total £12 billion annually.

# Liberal Democrats Manifesto 2024 Summary

The Liberal Democrats' 2024 manifesto centres on five key themes: economy, public services, environment, international relations, and democratic reform.

## Economy and Business

The party proposes investing in renewable energy and home insulation to reduce energy bills and create jobs. They would replace business rates with a Commercial Landowner Levy, expand apprenticeships, and introduce Lifelong Skills Grants of £5,000 for adult education. The manifesto commits to responsible fiscal management while repairing trade relationships with Europe. Tax proposals include reversing bank tax cuts, increasing the Digital Services Tax, and reforming capital gains tax.

## Health and Social Care

Central pledges include guaranteeing GP appointments within seven days (24 hours for urgent cases), recruiting 8,000 additional GPs, and ensuring NHS dental access for emergency care. Mental health provisions include walk-in hubs for young people and professionals in every school. The party proposes free personal care based on the Scottish model, a Royal College of Care Workers, and increased Carer's Allowance with expanded eligibility.

## Education

Proposals include placing mental health professionals in all schools, increasing per-pupil funding above inflation, providing tutoring guarantees for disadvantaged pupils, and reinstating maintenance grants for university students. Early years investment would include extra free hours for disadvantaged three and four-year-olds.

## Environment

The manifesto commits to net zero by 2045, with 90% renewable electricity by 2030. A ten-year home energy upgrade programme would provide free insulation and heat pumps for low-income households. Water companies would be transformed into public benefit companies, with bonuses banned until sewage discharges end. Targets include doubling protected areas, wildlife habitats, species abundance, and woodland cover by 2050.

## Housing

The party would build 380,000 homes annually, including 150,000 social homes, through new garden cities. Renters would receive protection through banned no-fault evictions and three-year default tenancies. Rough sleeping would be ended within the Parliament.

## Crime and Justice

Proposals include restoring community policing, guaranteeing police attendance at all burglaries, and creating an Online Crime Agency. Court backlogs would be addressed through increased investment, with rehabilitation programmes expanded to reduce reoffending.

## Immigration

The party would scrap the Rwanda scheme and Illegal Migration Act, establish safe legal routes for refugees, and process asylum claims within three months. Asylum seekers could work after three months of waiting. Work visa policy would move from the Home Office to relevant departments.

## Democratic Reform

Key reforms include introducing proportional representation (Single Transferable Vote) for MPs and English councillors, votes at 16, scrapping voter ID requirements, and capping political donations. The Ministerial Code would become law, and House of Lords reform would proceed.

## International Affairs

The manifesto prioritises repairing EU relations through a four-stage roadmap, ultimately aiming for Single Market membership. Defence spending would increase toward 2.5% of GDP, Army cuts would be reversed, and international development spending would return to 0.7% of national income. The party supports Ukraine and advocates for an immediate ceasefire in Gaza with recognition of Palestinian statehood.

## Families and Welfare

Proposals include extending free school meals to all children in poverty, doubling Statutory Maternity Pay to £350 weekly, and removing the two-child benefit limit. The triple lock on pensions would be maintained, and compensation for 1950s-born women would be delivered.
